_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401883110.overall: Bottom against top at the Alfonso Murube on Monday night (20:30 Spanish time): Ceuta are last with 5 points from 14 games (10 scored, 32 conceded) and have lost five in a row, while Almería have 32 points, 26 scored and 11 conceded, and are twelve games unbeaten in league and cup; Castellón's weekend win means they need to win here to go back top. Sergio Lobera, in his first full week and first home game in charge after a 2-0 loss at Tenerife, calls it a chance for a turning point, wants the Murube full (season-ticket holders get free tickets) and mentioned absences without naming anyone. Almería's squad list confirms captain Jorge Pulido is a late absence with an ankle problem, alongside Rodrigo Ely and Nico Melamed; only Melamed is in the numbers (about -6% on their goals), while Marcos Luna, Stefan Dzodic (back from a ban) and Brian Cipenga (back from international duty) return. Referee Eder Mallo Fernández, confirmed with Rubén Ávalos on VAR, gives about 5.5 cards a game, near the league average, and that record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, already taking about 6% off Almería for Melamed and adding a little to Ceuta from last season's 3-2 home win in this fixture. What they don't see is now confirmed: Almería lose centre-back and captain Pulido late (Ely is also out), which should help Ceuta's thin attack led by Jordi Escobar, while Almería get Dzodic and Cipenga back and must win to retake top spot. Both sides point slightly up, so a mild +3%, about 3.3 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 6.1 of them Ceuta's, already including their recent run of 44 corners in six games (+11% momentum). García Pimienta expects Ceuta to want the ball at home, which fits Lobera's possession style with high full-backs, and Almería with Cipenga back have more width on the break; none of this changes the corner count beyond what the numbers already see, so 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards, already counting Ceuta's heavy recent booking (+12% momentum) and referee Eder Mallo Fernández, whose 5.5 cards a game is close to the league average (+2.5%). A desperate home side in front of a full ground may foul to stop Almería's counters, but that is the pattern the numbers already see and there is no derby or other edge here, so I stay at 6.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.5 shots, with Ceuta's recent volume adding about 31% to their side and Almería's quieter attacking run taking about 7% off theirs. Lobera wants balance rather than all-out attack, and Almería without Pulido may concede a few more efforts but need few chances themselves; that sits within what the numbers already give, so 31.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. Ceuta hit the target only twice at Tenerife despite most of the ball and Lobera admits they score too little, which argues lower, but a reshuffled Almería back line without Pulido and Ely should make clean shots a little easier for them; those offset, so I stay at 10.3.

401875009.overall: Two struggling sides meet on Monday night: Monza are 18th with 7 points after four straight defeats, and Paolo Vanoli's Fiorentina are 15th with 9 points, unbeaten in three and scoring in ten straight games. Ivan Juric is banned and watches from the stands, so assistant Matteo Paro leads Monza; Juric asked for 'rage' against Fiorentina, and local press frame the game as one that could decide his future. Captain Pessina is back in the squad after three months out but will probably start on the bench, while Folorunsho (counted), Maye and Ngonge are out; Varela (9 goals in 10 games) leads the line. Fiorentina have Atta back in the squad for gradual minutes, Ndour recovered and Njie a late doubt with a thigh problem (Gnonto ready to start), with Pongracic and Parisi (both counted) out. Referee Daniele Doveri is one of Serie A's most lenient (2.7 cards a game), which the numbers already count.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already adding a little for both sides' recent scoring and leaky defending and taking about 4% off Fiorentina for Pongracic. Monza miss Ngonge and Maye, who are not in the numbers' list, but they have been out for weeks so recent form already reflects it, and top scorer Varela starts; Fiorentina have scored in ten straight games and get Atta and Ndour back. Nothing moves the total, so about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners, already nudging up for Fiorentina's recent corner count (32 in six). Monza's 3-4-2-1 with Birindelli and Mangas as wing-backs and Fiorentina's 4-2-3-1 with Mastantuono and Njie or Gnonto wide are both sides' usual shapes, so I stay at about 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, already cut by about 29% for Doveri's lenient record, which I don't size again. This is a relegation scrap between sides two points apart, with Juric banned, his job reportedly on the line and him publicly asking his players for 'rage'; that tends to bring more fouls than a usual Doveri match, so a mild lean up to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, already raised for both sides' recent shooting (+9% Monza, +14% Fiorentina). Monza need to attack at home and Fiorentina are close to full strength, but that is the picture the numbers already have, so about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, already lifted around 10% for each side's recent accuracy. Varela leads Monza's line with Mota and Robinson behind him, and Pellegrino leads Fiorentina's with Mastantuono and Gonçalves; nothing in the team news changes that, so about 10.

401879237.overall: Brentford (10th, 14 points, beaten 2-0 at Brighton before the break) host Everton (7th, 16 points, three straight wins in all competitions including 1-0 at Newcastle and a home win over Coventry) on Monday night, two points apart. Brentford are badly hit: Igor Thiago serves a ban after his red card at Brighton (the numbers count it, about -12.5% on their goals), Nathan Collins (knee) and Aaron Hickey (hamstring) are out for weeks, Rico Henry and Kaye Furo are sidelined, Dasilva and Milambo were only due a B-team run-out on Sunday, and Fabio Carvalho may make the squad; Callum Wilson is expected to lead the line. Everton report no new injuries, Moyes saying no one is ruled out, and are expected in their usual 4-2-3-1 with Thierno Barry (six league goals, the league's top xG) up front; Moyes becomes Everton's outright record holder for games managed tonight. Match-day checks found no change from this morning, and referee Craig Pawson (26 yellows and one red in six league games; 3.7 cards a game on record) is already counted, so the view stays as it was.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, already taking about 12.5% off Brentford for Thiago's ban. They count missing players only by goals and assists, so they barely feel the loss of first-choice defenders Collins and Hickey, which helps Barry, the league's top chance-getter and strong in the air against a Brentford back line that relies on aerial duels. Wilson starting and Carvalho's possible return soften Brentford's attacking loss, so I keep it mild: about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners, already counting Brentford's low recent corner count (21 in six) and Everton's slightly higher one. Brentford still play wide and cross a lot, with a stand-in on the left for Hickey, and Everton line up in their usual 4-2-3-1, so nothing on match day points away from 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already lowered about 10% for referee Craig Pawson's record and for calm past meetings. Everton have no suspensions and Moyes reports a fit squad, the table gap is two points and there is no rivalry between these clubs, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, already raising Everton for their recent volume (81 shots in six). Brentford lose Thiago's shooting but Wilson starts, while a weakened Brentford defence should let Everton's midfield trio of Armstrong, Garner and Dewsbury-Hall push on; the two roughly balance, so 27.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, already lowering Brentford for poor recent accuracy (19 on target in six). Losing Thiago's finishing is offset by Barry facing a back four without Collins and Hickey, so I stay at 8.2.

401882802.overall: A Monday-night Valencian relegation derby: Levante (18th, 11 points) host Elche (19th, 10 points), so the winner climbs past the other and possibly out of the drop zone. Luís Castro has the whole Levante squad available, with Manu Sánchez back from a hamstring injury and only Nakoha listed as a doubt. Martín Anselmi's Elche miss playmaker Marc Aguado (ankle), Adam Boayar and Yago, none of whom the numbers list (they only take off Ali Houary), while Villar, Sangaré and Lemar are back in training, Revivo was a midweek doubt and Cepeda returned late from Chile; Elche have lost their last two without scoring. Referee Francisco José Hernández Maeso (4.2 cards a game) is already counted, but the numbers do not flag the derby or the relegation stakes; no confirmed lineups yet at this refresh, so the view from this morning holds with the card lean trimmed slightly.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, high for two bottom-three sides, and their momentum trims Elche only slightly even though they have failed to score in their last two. Elche are without Marc Aguado, who runs their midfield and is not in the numbers, and a six-pointer between sides a point apart tends to be cautious; a mild lean down to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, 4.9 of them Levante's, and already count Elche's recent 31 corners in six games. Levante should take the initiative at home with Manu Sánchez back on the left, while Elche keep the ball and cross; nothing in the team news shifts that, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, already including referee Hernández Maeso (about -12% for his 4.2 a game) and Levante's light recent booking count, which I don't size again. What they don't flag is that this is a regional derby and a direct relegation fight between sides a point apart, which usually brings more fouls and bookings; a moderate lean up to about 4.1, a touch below this morning's view because cards takes have run hot lately.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.5 shots and already add for both sides' recent shooting, with Levante conceding 103 in their last six. Levante with Iván Romero and Etta Eyong should press at home, but a nervy six-pointer could slow the game; nothing points clearly either way, so 29.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Levante have a full squad, and Elche's recent blanks are more about finishing than about getting shots on target, which the numbers' momentum already reflects; without Aguado their supply may dip a little, but not enough to move, so 8.9.

401915380.overall: Bodø/Glimt are 25th of 36 with 4 points, both earned at home (1-0 against Dortmund, 0-0 against Lille), so this game on the Aspmyra artificial pitch is close to a must-win for the play-off places; they lead the Norwegian league and have won 14 of their last 15 league games. LASK are 16th with 6 points and arrive on five straight league wins, but vice-captain Andrés Andrade (ankle) is out, and the numbers now count him (+6.2% on Bodø's goals). Florian Flecker (calf), one of LASK's joint top Champions League scorers, is also out and is still not counted; Bello and Harakaté are out and counted, as are Evjen (knee) and Mikkelsen (groin) for Bodø. Line-ups are due an hour before kick-off and the match-day previews still show the same expected XIs as this morning, with Usor up front for LASK and Hauge and Blomberg wide for Bodø. Turkish referee Halil Umut Meler, whose higher card rate is already counted, is in charge on a cold night under floodlights.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.0 goals (2.9 Bodø, 1.1 LASK); since this morning they also count Andrade's absence (+6.2% for Bodø), plus LASK's hot scoring run (+2.8%) and Evjen, Mikkelsen and Bello. What they still cannot see is Flecker, one of LASK's main Champions League scorers, missing from every predicted XI, and Bodø's two home games in this competition produced one goal in total. I keep -4%, about 3.8 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, 5.9 of them for Bodø as the side expected to have the ball, with both teams' recent corner counts (+0.8% and -1.0%) already in. LASK's 3-5-2 with wing-backs Jørgensen and Dibango and Bodø's wide attack through Blomberg and Hauge are both confirmed in today's predicted line-ups, which is what the numbers expect, so I stay at 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already adding referee Halil Umut Meler's 4.5 cards a game (+7.5%) and taking off LASK's low recent card count (-6.6%) and Bodø's (-2.1%). There is no rivalry; a reshuffled LASK back three without Andrade on a fast artificial pitch, which Kühbauer calls an extra challenge, may be stretched a little, but that is a normal away-team picture, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots (14.4 Bodø, 12.5 LASK), already trimmed for Bodø's quieter recent shooting (-3.9%). Bodø need the win and will push, while Kühbauer says LASK want to take something home and will still play two strikers without Flecker; these pull both ways, so I stay at 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, already counting LASK's sharp recent finishing (+3.9%) and Bodø's slight dip (-2.0%). The LASK absences (Andrade at the back, Flecker up front) roughly cancel for shots on target, and I have put the net effect into goals rather than counting it twice, so I stay at 10.5.

401915300.overall: Galatasaray are 18th of 36 with 6 points and Aston Villa 6th with 9; Galatasaray have won their last two Champions League games (Lille, Stuttgart) and want a top-24 place, while Villa lost 3-0 at Barcelona last time and Emery admits a top-8 finish is out of their hands. Osimhen, Leão and Sallai are out and the numbers count all three on goals; Sporx's match-day page still lists Osimhen as injured, with Jakobs a doubt, and the predicted XIs have no recognised centre-forward: Barış Alper Yılmaz, Yunus Akgün and Batrakov in attack with Lemina beside Torreira. Villa are without Cash, Ruggeri and Onana (all counted); Lindelöf was a doubt with illness, so Harwood-Bellis is expected alongside Pau Torres. Line-ups come an hour before kick-off and nothing has changed since this morning. German referee Daniel Siebert, average on cards and already counted, is in charge on a repaired RAMS Park pitch.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals (1.1 Galatasaray, 1.8 Villa) and already take off Osimhen (-10%), Sallai and Leão (-5% each) from Galatasaray's goals, plus Cash for Villa. The striker-less plan is just the other side of Osimhen's absence; one report says he might sit on the bench, but at most for a late cameo, so nothing new moves the total and I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners, already counting Galatasaray's slight rise in corners won (+2.9%) and Villa's dip (-3.4%). Villa keep the ball and push wide with Maatsen and Wan-Bissaka, while Galatasaray lose width without Leão and Sallai and, in today's Turkish line-ups, play Lemina in a more solid midfield; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, with Galatasaray's quieter recent card count (-8.4%), Villa's slight rise (+3.7%) and Daniel Siebert's average record (4.1 a game, +1%) already in. RAMS Park is loud and both sides need points, and a patched pitch can bring a few clumsy challenges, but that is close to a normal Champions League night here, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots (12.8 Galatasaray, 13.7 Villa); they take the missing forwards off goals but not off shots. With Osimhen, Sallai and Leão all out, no centre-forward in the predicted XI and Lemina added as a second holding midfielder, Galatasaray lose their main shot-takers, and a repaired pitch may slow the game; I keep the trim, to about 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target, already counting Villa's sharper recent finishing (+5.9%) and Galatasaray's slight dip (-0.8%), but not the forwards Galatasaray are missing. Osimhen is the player who turns their chances into efforts on target and he will not start, so I keep my lean lower, to about 9.7.

401915295.overall: Arsenal are 3rd in the league phase on 10 points and top of the Premier League despite Saturday's 2-2 draw at Newcastle; Dortmund are 12th on 9 points and top of the Bundesliga. Match-day previews confirm David Raya is out with the shoulder he hurt at Newcastle (no surgery needed), so Kepa starts in goal, and Zubimendi (hamstring) and Saka (quad) are also out; the numbers count Saka (about -10% on Arsenal's goals) and Raya, but not Zubimendi. Sports Mole expects Gyokeres, White, Hincapie and Lewis-Skelly back in the XI, with Saliba still not fit to start. For Dortmund, Emre Can, Inacio, Konstantelias, Lerma and Kaba are out; Guirassy is in the squad but UEFA still lists him doubtful with a thigh problem, so Fabio Silva or Beier is expected to lead the line. Italian referee Maurizio Mariani, slightly below average on cards, is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals; they already take about 10% off Arsenal for Saka and add a little to Dortmund for Raya's absence. Arsenal also miss Zubimendi's control in midfield, which the numbers don't count, and Dortmund have Guirassy available at least from the bench, so I stay a touch higher: 2.5 x 1.02, about 2.55.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, with Arsenal around 6.3 and Dortmund's busier recent corner count already in (+3.0%). Arsenal build corners from sustained pressure and set pieces even without Saka, with Madueke and Eze expected wide, and Dortmund tend to defend deep away in a back three; both records already show this, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards, already adding about 13% to Arsenal for their high recent card count and trimming a little for Maurizio Mariani, who averages 3.9 cards a game against a 4.1 average. There are no bans and no needle between the clubs, so nothing new points either way; I stay at 3.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots, with Dortmund's busy recent shooting already counted (+11.3%) and Arsenal's (+5.7%). Gyokeres is expected back up front for Arsenal, but they still miss Saka's output on the right and Zubimendi's control, while Guirassy is at best a substitute for Dortmund. These roughly cancel, so I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target, including a small boost for Dortmund's recent accuracy (+2.7%). Guirassy, Dortmund's most clinical finisher, is still listed doubtful and likely starts on the bench, and Arsenal have been less incisive without Saka, so nothing clearly moves it; I stay at 8.6.

401915296.overall: Como are 4th on 9 points in their first Champions League season and beat Cagliari 2-0 on Saturday; AEK are 29th on 3 points and need a result. Kean, Diao, Addai and Jesus Rodriguez are out for Como, but today's previews (UEFA, The Stats Zone) list Caqueret only as a doubt rather than out, Chalobah is fit again and Fabregas is expected to field Da Cunha, Nico Paz and Baturina behind Douvikas, so Como's attack looks stronger than it did this morning. The numbers take a little off for Diao and Kean and ride Como's 17 goals in six games. AEK travel without the suspended Koita and Zubkov (Arriaga is listed out by UEFA, though one preview still has him in the XI), and Fabregas calls them physical and dominant. Spanish referee Javier Alberola Rojas, who has averaged about 4.7 yellows a game this season, is in charge.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already trimming Como for Diao and Kean while adding 4.3% for their recent scoring. Caqueret is now only doubtful and Nico Paz, Baturina and Da Cunha are expected to start, so I soften this morning's -5; what is left is Como without natural wingers and AEK without Koita, a UEFA ban the numbers don't know about: 2.9 x 0.97, about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, with Como around 5.6 and both sides' small recent dips already in. Without natural wingers Como's width comes from full-backs Valle and Couto, who already supplied much of it, and AEK are likely to defend deep away from home; nothing clearly moves the count, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and already take about 16% off Como for how few cards they have picked up lately, plus 7% off AEK. Alberola Rojas has shown about 4.7 yellows a game this season, a little busier than average, and Fabregas calls AEK physical, but the referee's record and AEK's style are already in the numbers, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.4 shots, with small recent dips counted on both sides. Como are still short of forwards (Kean, Diao, Addai and Rodriguez out) and AEK lose Koita, one of their most frequent shooters, whom the numbers still count; with Paz and Baturina expected to start I keep the trim small: 25.4 x 0.98, about 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target, with Como's sharp recent finishing counted. Koita's ban removes much of AEK's threat from wide, which the numbers don't see, and Como rely on Douvikas alone up front, though their creative midfielders are fit, so I go slightly lower: 9.3 x 0.97, about 9.0.

401915294.overall: Both sides have 3 points: Feyenoord are 32nd and Porto 26th, and both need wins to stay in the race for the top 24. Feyenoord are six games without a win after Saturday's 3-2 home defeat to Excelsior and have conceded eight in their last two league games, leaving Giovanni van Bronckhorst under pressure; Hadj Moussa is in the predicted XI after an ankle knock, but centre-back Watanabe is a doubt with a foot problem (not in the numbers), and St. Juste, Bos, Nieuwkoop, Beelen and Moder are out, St. Juste already counted. Porto lead the Portuguese league by five points, unbeaten in 11, and beat Napoli 4-1 last time out in Europe; Smalling is not in their Champions League squad and William Gomes is back in training but uncertain. Farioli expects a physical game with many duels and wants to press high. Bosnian referee Irfan Peljto, who gives fewer cards than average over his career, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already add a little to Porto for St. Juste's absence. Two sides who both need a win, a Feyenoord defence that has leaked eight in two league games and may also lose Watanabe, and a Porto side planning to press high point to an open game: 2.9 x 1.03, about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners, with Feyenoord's lower recent count already in (-4.0%). Feyenoord usually have most of the ball at home and Hadj Moussa's dribbling helps them win corners, while Porto's full-backs push high; that is in both normal records, so I stay at 8.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards and count Irfan Peljto's low card rate (-9.2%) and both sides' calm recent discipline. Farioli expects a physical game full of duels, which could add a booking, but Peljto lets a lot go over his career, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots and already add about 13% to Porto for how many shots Feyenoord have been conceding. Both teams must chase a win and Porto want to win the ball high, which tends to create quick shots on both sides: 26.3 x 1.02, about 26.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, including a 12.6% boost for Porto from Feyenoord's poor recent defending and a 4.7% cut for Feyenoord's poor finishing. With Hadj Moussa expected to start and Porto in form in front of goal, in a game both need to win, I go slightly up: 9.6 x 1.02, about 9.8.

401915379.overall: Manchester City are 7th on 9 points but come in on four Premier League games without a win after Saturday's 1-1 home draw with Fulham, with Arsenal away on Sunday; Maresca wants a top-eight finish. Only Semenyo is out (already counted) and Matheus Nunes is fit again; today's previews expect only limited rotation, with Haaland, Doku and Cherki starting and Khusanov at right-back. Allegri's Napoli, 27th on 3 points, are without Buongiorno (meniscus), Di Lorenzo, Lobotka, Meret, Badiashile, Vergara and Alisson Santos, and Rafa Marin is suspended, leaving Rrahmani and Beukema as the only fit specialist centre-backs; reports differ on whether Neres is fit. The numbers count Lobotka, Di Lorenzo, Vergara and Rafa Marin but not Buongiorno. Romanian referee Istvan Kovacs, an average carder, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and already take off for Semenyo, Di Lorenzo, Lobotka, Vergara and the suspended Rafa Marin. They do not know Buongiorno is also out, leaving Napoli with two fit specialist centre-backs against Haaland, and today's previews expect City to rotate less than feared this morning, so I go a little further: 3.4 x 1.05, about 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, mostly City's, and already add about 10% for how many corners Napoli have conceded lately. With a patched-up defence Napoli should be pinned back even more than their record shows, and blocked crosses from Doku and Ndiaye turn into corners: a mild lean up, to about 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, with Napoli's busier recent card count (+12%) and Istvan Kovacs's average record included, so I do not lean on the referee. What is left is a stand-in Napoli back line, likely with Politano at right-back, chasing City's wingers and likely to give away fouls: a small lean up, to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.6 shots and already add about 13% to City for the volume Napoli have been allowing. Buongiorno's absence is not in that figure, and with Haaland, Doku and Cherki expected to start City should have even more of the ball, so I go up a bit more than this morning: 28.6 x 1.04, about 29.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, with Napoli's sharp recent finishing (+8%) already counted. A weakened Napoli back line should let City shoot from closer in, and City's attack is expected near full strength, though they managed little against Fulham, so I keep the move small: 10.4 x 1.04, about 10.8.

401915299.overall: RB Leipzig (30th) and Lens (33rd) both have 3 points from four games and need a win to stay in the race for the top 24; Leipzig are 4th in the Bundesliga under Martin Demichelis after a 5-1 win at Union Berlin, Lens drew 1-1 with Toulouse in Didier Digard's first game after the 9-1 loss at Como. Leipzig centre-back Castello Lukeba (bruised knee) missed the final training session and is out, and he is not on the numbers' missing list, so Orban and Esteve are expected to pair at the back; Ouedraogo and Guiu are still out (counted). Three French outlets expect a back three with Ganiou and Abdulhamid wide, Haidara and Titraoui in midfield and Thauvin, Hazard and Sima in attack. Slovak referee Ivan Kruzliak, a little below average on cards, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, already adding about 8% to Leipzig for their recent scoring and taking a little off Lens for Cuisance and Edouard. Lukeba's absence is confirmed today but is not in the numbers, so a reshuffled Leipzig back line faces a Lens front three of Thauvin, Hazard and the returning Sima. A small nudge up: 3.5 x 1.03, about 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, split fairly evenly, with small recent dips counted on both sides. Lens are expected in a back three with a centre-back, Ganiou, at left wing-back and Aguilar out on the right, so they look less of a crossing side, while Leipzig still go wide through Nusa and Raum. That balances out, so I stay at 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, with Leipzig's quieter recent record (-8%) and Ivan Kruzliak's slightly low card rate (-5.4%) counted. Both sides need the win and Demichelis expects a strong reaction from Lens after the Como defeat, but there is no history of bad blood and no ban in play, so I stay at 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.5 shots, adding about 7% to Leipzig for their busy recent shooting and trimming Lens (-9%) for their low count. Lens lose Cuisance and Edouard but get Sima back up front, and Leipzig miss Lukeba at the back rather than any attacker, so the volume of shooting should look like the numbers expect. I stay at 28.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.5 shots on target and already add about 15% to Leipzig for how often they have tested goalkeepers lately. The one thing they cannot see is Lukeba's absence, which should make it a little easier for Lens to get shots away cleanly, so a slight nudge: 11.5 x 1.02, about 11.7.

401915298.overall: Real Madrid are 2nd on a perfect 12 points under Jose Mourinho and have won nine in a row, the last 2-1 against Celta; Vinicius starts (his domestic ban does not apply in Europe) and Valverde and Tchouameni return after being rested. Rodrygo and Endrick are out (counted), Asencio is injured, Mendy is not registered, and Dumfries, though in the squad list, missed Monday's training and is not expected to play; most previews have Guler and Bellingham starting, one has Brahim in. PSV are 24th on 4 points and lead the Eredivisie, but Mauro Junior is out (counted) with 18-year-old Noah Fernandez expected to replace him, Dest is a doubt and Schouten, Nagalo, Plea and Ouaissa remain out. Norwegian referee Espen Eskas, an average carder, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say a high 4.5 goals, built on Madrid's strong recent scoring and PSV's open style under Bosz, and they already take a little off PSV for Mauro Junior. Madrid's front line of Mbappe, Vinicius and Bellingham is expected to start, and PSV keep their attack of Perisic, Mijnans, Van Bommel and Til, so nothing new changes the picture. I stay at 4.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners and already trim PSV (-6%) for their low recent count against strong defences. Valverde back at right-back adds width for Madrid and Perisic and Van Bommel give PSV wide threat, which is their normal shape and already in the records, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, close to both teams' usual rates, and include Espen Eskas, whose record is about average. A young PSV midfield with Fernandez in for the captain may have to foul to stop Madrid's runners, but that is a guess, there is no needle between the clubs and no ban in play, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.0 shots, including Madrid's heavy recent shooting (+4.8%). Mourinho talked of rotating, but today's previews still have Bellingham, Guler or Brahim, Vinicius and Mbappe behind a first-choice midfield, while PSV are a little weaker in midfield without Mauro Junior. Nothing is big enough to move, so I stay at 31.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.7 on target, with Madrid's sharp recent finishing counted (+8%). Mbappe and Vinicius both start and PSV keep their usual attacking set-up, possibly without Dest at right-back, which is roughly what the numbers assume, so I stay at 12.7.

401915297.overall: Slovan Bratislava are bottom of the league phase with no points and a 1-17 goal record after 12 straight European defeats, though they beat Ruzomberok 1-0 on Saturday under Yaya Toure. Slovan are without Suleiman Camara (counted, a big cut to their goals), Mustafic and Medvedev, with Wimmer, Gajdos and Cerepkai doubtful. Betis are 11th on 9 points and 4th in La Liga after a 1-1 derby draw with Sevilla; Ceballos and Morante are out (counted), Lo Celso is out with a knee knock from training, and Pellegrini is expected to make seven or eight changes before Saturday's game with Rayo, with Parrott up front and Cucho only fit for minutes off the bench. French referee Jerome Brisard, about average on cards, is in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already cut Slovan's share hard (about -37%) for Camara's absence, so I do not count that again. What they cannot see is Betis's heavy rotation: seven or eight changes, Lo Celso out, Parrott leading the line and Cucho only off the bench. A small trim: 2.9 x 0.96, about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, with Betis around 6.1 and their busy recent corner counts already in (+3%). Even a rotated Betis should dominate the ball with Antony, Abde or Riquelme on the wings while Slovan defend deep, which is already in both records, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, reflecting Slovan's usual card rate when chasing the ball, and Jerome Brisard's about-average record is already counted. Betis are a technical side, the game has no history and nothing points to more heat than usual, so I stay at 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.8 shots and add about 11% to Betis for how much Slovan concede. A Betis side with seven or eight changes and no Lo Celso may play at a lower tempo once ahead, and Slovan's own shooting at this level has been thin with Gajdos doubtful. A slight trim: 31.8 x 0.97, about 30.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, including a 6% boost for Betis and already a lower Slovan figure without Camara. Betis start with second-choice attackers such as Parrott and Riquelme, and Slovan rarely test goalkeepers in this competition, so I go to 10.5 x 0.96, about 10.1.

401915378.overall: Sabah are 30th of 36 with 3 points in their first Champions League campaign and Barcelona 8th with 9, so Barcelona need the win to stay in the top-eight race, at the Olympic Stadium in Baku. Barcelona are without Lamine Yamal (ankle, kept at home as a precaution), Rodri, Christensen, Espart and Bardghji, and a team-news page today lists Kounde and Olmo as doubts; the numbers count Yamal, Christensen and Espart only. Flick said Cubarsi can play if needed and previews expect a rotated side with Gavi or Bernal, Fermin, Adeyemi and Gordon around Raphinha and Pedri. Sabah lose centre-back Aden McCarthy to a red-card ban (counted) and leading scorer Simic is a doubt; one team-news page says Mickels is banned for yellow cards while another predicted line-up still starts him, so that stays unclear. Scottish referee Nick Walsh, who shows a lot of cards, is in charge and the numbers already add about a quarter to cards for him; line-ups were not out when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.4 goals (1.1 Sabah, 3.4 Barcelona), already taking off Yamal (-16.7%), Espart and Christensen for Barcelona and McCarthy for Sabah, and counting both sides' good scoring runs. What they can't see is Flick's rotation, Olmo and Kounde being doubts, and Sabah's top scorer Simic (and possibly Mickels) missing, so I trim a little, to about 4.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, 6.6 of them for Barcelona, who should have most of the ball against a Sabah side that likes to play out from the back but will spend long spells defending. Without Yamal the width comes from Adeyemi and Gordon with Cancelo pushing on, so play still goes down the flanks, and the changes are mostly in defence and midfield, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, already adding Nick Walsh's high card rate (+26%; about five yellows a game in his two games this season) and Sabah's busy recent card record (+11%), and taking a little off for Barcelona's quieter run. That is already a high figure for a game with no rivalry and nothing new on discipline turned up, so I stay at 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.5 shots (8.9 Sabah, 25.6 Barcelona), lifted for both sides' heavy recent shooting. Yamal is one of Barcelona's main shooters and the numbers take his absence only off goals, Flick is rotating with Olmo doubtful, and Sabah may lack Simic up front, so I lean lower, to about 33.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target, 9.0 for Barcelona, already lifted for their recent accuracy (+8.5%). Without Yamal and with a rotated side the quality of Barcelona's chances should dip a little, and Sabah's attack is thinner if Simic misses out, so I trim to about 11.8.

401915293.overall: Slavia are 34th of 36 with 1 point and Villarreal 29th with 3, so both are below the top-24 line and need a win; Villarreal coach Inigo Perez called it decisive and blamed Saturday's 3-2 loss at Barcelona, after leading 2-0, on mentality. Slavia are without Sturm, Chaloupek, Pitak, Ouanda and Ogbu, all counted (Sturm alone takes about a quarter off their goals), and two previews today add midfielder David Moses injured and Lukas Provod a doubt, which the numbers don't list; neither preview has striker Chory in the side. Villarreal miss Saliba (ankle surgery) and Diatta, both counted, while Gerard Moreno is back in the squad and Foyth and Akhomach are back in training; the earlier report of Mourino being banned is not backed today, with both predicted line-ups starting him. Perez called Slavia the most aggressive side in the competition, and Slovenian referee Rade Obrenovic, with a slightly low card record, is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals (0.9 Slavia, 2.4 Villarreal), already cutting Slavia hard for Sturm and the other injured players. Moses out and Provod doubtful thin Slavia's attack further, but Gerard Moreno's return gives Villarreal an extra option the numbers don't count, so I lean only slightly lower than before, to about 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, fairly even (4.1 Slavia, 5.1 Villarreal), with Slavia's recent corner run counted. Slavia play a direct, wing-back game and must attack at home, Villarreal go wide through Buchanan and Moleiro, and the absences change little here, so I stay at 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards, taking a little off for Obrenovic's slightly low card record and Slavia's calmer recent run. Perez expects Slavia's usual aggression and both sides need the win, but that intensity is part of Slavia's long record the numbers already use, and the Mourino ban did not hold up, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots, lifted for Slavia's heavy recent shooting (+15.9%). With Moses out and Provod doubtful, Slavia lose two midfielders who shoot and create, which the numbers can't see, so I trim to about 30.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 on target, with Slavia's recent accuracy counted (+11.3%). A thinner Slavia midfield points to slightly fewer good chances, partly offset by Gerard Moreno's return for Villarreal, so I lean a touch lower, to about 9.9.

401915291.overall: Atletico Madrid (26th, 4 points) and Viking (25th, 4 points) sit one place apart in the clubs' first meeting, and Atletico, after losing to Liverpool and Bayern, need to win at home to keep any hope of the top eight. Atletico beat Getafe 3-0 on Sunday; Lookman and Cuti Romero are out and counted, Marc Pubill has recovered from his ankle sprain according to two Spanish reports, Hjulmand is back from his European ban, and one report says Sorloth was left out of the squad, with Kang-in Lee or Baena next to Julian Alvarez. Viking, three points behind Bodo/Glimt in the Norwegian title race after losing 3-2 at Tromso, miss Bjorshol, D'Agostino, Roseth and Baertelsen (counted), and an illness has hit the squad: left-back Kristoffer Haugen is out and top scorer Peter Christiansen is still a doubt, neither on the numbers' list. Belgian referee Erik Lambrechts (about 2.9 cards a game) is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals (2.6 Atletico, 1.2 Viking), with only small cuts for Lookman and Romero. Viking's illness is not on their list: Haugen is missing at left-back and Christiansen is doubtful, and Viking have already conceded 10 in four Champions League games, so their defence looks weaker than the numbers assume. Pubill being fit again and Sorloth possibly missing pull a little the other way, so I keep a small lean higher, to about 3.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.6 corners, 8.0 for Atletico, who should pin Viking back, with momentum already counted on both sides. Atletico's width comes from Giuliano Simeone, Llorente and Grimaldo whoever plays up front, and a makeshift Viking left side changes little to the total, so I stay at 11.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.9 cards, already taking about 16% off for Lambrechts' low card rate and both sides' calm recent runs. There is no rivalry, Viking play an open, passing game and nothing in the news points to a nastier match, so I stay at 2.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.9 shots (21.0 Atletico, 9.9 Viking), already lifted for Viking's busy recent shooting. Viking's illness could cut their shots a little while Atletico should dominate even more, which roughly cancels out, so I stay at 30.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 on target, 7.6 for Atletico. Julian Alvarez leads the line whether Sorloth or Kang-in Lee partners him, and Viking's threat depends on whether Christiansen shakes off his illness, so nothing clearly moves this; I stay at 10.8.

401915292.overall: Club Brugge and Liverpool are level on 9 points in the top-ten area, so the winner moves close to the top eight. Ivan Leko's Brugge are unbeaten in 11 and won 2-1 at PSV in their last European game; Joel Ordonez is out and winger Jan Virgili is back in training but short of fitness, both counted, and Tresoldi is set to lead the line after a mild concussion on U21 duty. Andoni Iraola's Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 on Sunday but lost 3-2 at Fenerbahce in their last European game; Ekitike is out and Gakpo and Gravenberch are unlikely (all counted), Leoni and Bradley are still out, and two previews (Vavel, Sports Mole) expect rotation with Lewis Koumas up front instead of Alexander Isak, while Rotowire still has Isak starting. Spanish referee Alejandro Hernandez Hernandez gives a lot of cards and the numbers already add about 29% to cards for him.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, split evenly, already taking off Gakpo (-8.3%) and Gravenberch and counting both sides' scoring runs. What they can't see is the expected rotation: two previews have Koumas leading the line with Munoz on a wing instead of Isak, which makes Liverpool's attack a bit less sharp, so I trim slightly, to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, 6.2 for Liverpool, already lifted for Liverpool's busy recent run. Without Gakpo, Liverpool's width comes from Barcola, Munoz and the full-backs, which still pushes play wide, and Brugge's Forbs and Lemarechal attack the flanks too, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already adding about 29% for Hernandez Hernandez's high card rate and Brugge's recent bookings. It is a close game with a lot at stake but no rivalry, and nothing new on discipline turned up, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 35.0 shots, already lifted for both sides' heavy recent shooting (+15% and +19%). Both teams press and attack, and a rotated Liverpool front line shoots about as often even if less well, so I stay at 35.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.8 on target, with both sides' recent accuracy counted. Brugge's Tresoldi is in form and Liverpool still have Wirtz, Barcola and Szoboszlai; any rotation dent is small and already reflected in my goals trim, so I stay at 11.8.

401915376.overall: Inter (17th, 6 points) and Stuttgart (15th, 7 points) both want to climb towards the top eight; Inter have won their last two in Europe after losing to Real Madrid and Brugge. Inter drew 4-4 at Atalanta on Sunday after leading by two, with Pio Esposito scoring a hat-trick; Calhanoglu, Zielinski and Bonny are out and all three are counted, and today's Italian previews (Tuttosport, Goal, LaPresse) all have Marcus Thuram starting next to Esposito, with Lautaro Martinez on the bench, so Thuram's fitness doubt from this morning has eased. Stuttgart drew 0-0 at Schalke; Sauer and Jaquez are out (counted), and Angelo Stiller is still unclear: two previews have him starting, Goal says his groin problem keeps him out. French referee Francois Letexier (about 4 cards a game) is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals (1.9 Inter, 1.2 Stuttgart), already taking off Calhanoglu, Zielinski and Bonny. This morning I trimmed for Thuram's fitness, but three previews now have him starting with the in-form Esposito and Lautaro available from the bench, while Inter's defence just conceded four at Atalanta, so I drop the trim and stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, 6.2 for Inter, already lifted for Inter's recent corner run. Inter's wing-backs Dimarco and Spence or Diouf drive a lot of corners, and Stuttgart's Leweling and Fuhrich attack wide too, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, with Letexier's average record barely moving them and Inter's calm recent run counted. There is no rivalry and nothing in the news points to a rougher game, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.8 shots, 21.5 for Inter after a big lift for their recent shooting (+19.9%). Inter will shoot a lot at home with Thuram and Esposito up front, and Stuttgart's output depends on whether Stiller plays, which is unclear, so I stay at 32.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 on target, lifted for Inter's recent accuracy. With Thuram now expected to start and Lautaro on the bench, Inter's finishing looks close to normal, so I drop this morning's small trim and stay at 10.6.

401915377.overall: Lille are 35th of 36 with 1 point from 4 games after a 1-0 home defeat to Lyon, so they need a result tonight to keep any play-off hope, while Bayern are 14th with 8 points. Lille miss Tiago Santos, Igamane and Nianzou (all counted by the numbers); this morning's predicted line-ups now have striker Ayase Ueda starting up front with Ethan Mbappe and Haraldsson behind him, so the earlier worry about Ueda has eased. Bayern are badly hit: Kane, Olise, Neuer, Davies, Gnabry and Saibari are out and counted, and reports say Kompany has ruled Musiala and Luis Diaz out of the starting side (Diaz trained but has not played since late October), so a young attack around Lennart Karl, Tom Bischof, Nathaniel Brown and Tim Binder is expected. Italian referee Marco Guida (about 3.6 cards a game) is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, already cutting Bayern hard for Kane (-15%), Olise (-14%), Saibari and Gnabry, and Lille for Tiago Santos. They can't see that Musiala and Diaz will not start, so Bayern's attack is a group of youngsters rather than their usual stars; Ueda is now expected to start for Lille, so I trim my earlier cut slightly and lean lower to about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners (4.6 Lille, 5.3 Bayern), with both sides' recent corner counts slightly below their usual level. Bayern will still have most of the ball with Laimer and Stanisic pushing up, and Lille have to attack at home, so nothing points away from the numbers; I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.0 cards, already taking about 12% off for Guida's lowish record and another 12% for Bayern's calm recent run. Lille's need for a result could bring a few more fouls late on, but nothing specific in the news points to a rough game, so I stay at 3.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.2 shots (10.3 Lille, 14.9 Bayern), and they take Bayern's absences off goals only, not shots, while lifting Bayern for their recent shooting. Without Kane, Olise, Musiala and Diaz in the starting side Bayern lose most of their usual shooters; with Ueda back in Lille's expected side I cut a little less than before, to about 23.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 on target, 5.4 of them Bayern's. A young Bayern front line built around Karl, Brown and Bischof should create fewer clean chances than the side the numbers rate, while Lille's attack is close to what the numbers expect, so I lean lower to about 8.6.

401915374.overall: PSG are 2nd of the league phase with 12 points from 4 games and four straight European wins; Roma are 23rd with 4 points and need results, though they are flying in Serie A. The fitness doubt from this morning has cleared: PSG's 23-man squad includes Dembele, Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes, with Digne and Boly also back, and Le Parisien and L'Equipe both expect Dembele to start up front with Akliouche and Mayulu or Godts. PSG still miss Doue and Kvaratskhelia (both counted); Roma miss Pellegrini and Rensch (counted) plus Bah, and are expected to line up 3-4-2-1 with Svilar in goal and Malen up front. Swedish referee Glenn Nyberg (about 3.5 cards a game) is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals (2.2 PSG, 1.4 Roma), already taking Doue and Kvaratskhelia off PSG and lifting both sides for strong scoring runs (PSG 21 and Roma 22 goals in their last 6). Dembele, Marquinhos and Mendes are now confirmed in the squad, which is what the numbers assumed, and Roma's in-form Malen leads their attack, so I stay at 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, 5.4 for PSG. PSG should have most of the ball against Gasperini's man-marking 3-4-2-1, which is already in both sides' records, and Roma's high recent corner count is counted too, so I stay at 9.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already taking 10% off for Nyberg's record and more for PSG's very calm recent run (3 cards in 6 games). Roma's man-to-man pressing brings fouls, but that is part of their record and nothing new points to a rougher night, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.3 shots, 21.6 for PSG, lifted for both sides' recent shooting. With Dembele back to lead the line PSG's shot volume should hold up even without Doue and Kvaratskhelia, and Roma's open style gives chances at both ends, so I stay at 32.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 13.2 on target, already lifted a lot for PSG's recent accuracy (+22%). This morning I held back because Dembele's fitness was unclear; he is now in the squad and expected to start, which matches what the numbers assume, so I stay at 13.2.

401915375.overall: Shakhtar (24th, 4 points) host Fenerbahce (22nd, 5 points) at Stamford Bridge in London because of the war, so there is little real home advantage, and both need points to stay in play-off contention. It is the first Champions League meeting of two Turkish head coaches, Arda Turan and Emre Belozoglu, who took over Fenerbahce on 3 November and is in his first Champions League game; Fenerbahce have not won away in this competition in 13 tries. Shakhtar are winless in three and miss Pedrinho, Gleiker Mendoza, Kaua Elias, Eguinaldo and Marlon Santos, all counted, and are expected to start Alisson Santana, Marlon Gomes, Newertton and Luca Meirelles in attack. Fenerbahce's 22-man squad is without only Ake and Asensio (counted); Turkish reports have Kante back alongside Guendouzi and Muriqi starting ahead of Lukaku, with Greenwood on the wing. English referee Michael Oliver (about 4 cards a game) is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals (0.8 Shakhtar, 1.6 Fenerbahce), already cutting Shakhtar hard for Pedrinho and Mendoza and taking Asensio and Ake into account for Fenerbahce. Today's squad news only confirms those absences, and Muriqi for Lukaku changes who scores more than how many, so I stay at 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, 5.3 for Shakhtar, already lifted for their recent corner run and cut for Fenerbahce's. A near-neutral venue and an open game with both sides needing points fit that figure, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, the highest of tonight's games, with Michael Oliver's close-to-average record barely moving them. Turan has asked for aggression and energy and both sides need the points, but that busy-game picture is already in both teams' card records, so I stay at 4.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots, lifted 15% for Shakhtar's recent shooting and cut 9% for Fenerbahce's quieter run. Kante's return should give Fenerbahce more control and Muriqi is a target man rather than a volume shooter, which changes the style more than the count, so I stay at 26.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 on target, almost even between the sides. Shakhtar lack their main finishers, which the numbers count through goals, and Fenerbahce's expected side with Greenwood and Muriqi is close to their usual one, so I stay at 8.8.

401915373.overall: Sporting (12th, 9 points, five wins in a row in all competitions) host Manchester United (19th, 6 points); a win would put Sporting near the top eight, while United need points to stay in the play-off spots. Both have new coaches: Paulo Fonseca at Sporting, who said United are hard to read and expects to spend spells in a mid-to-low block and counter-attack, and Mauricio Pochettino at United, whose first game was a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool. United are without Matheus Cunha (one-match UEFA ban for his red card against Roma, confirmed by ESPN and others), whom the numbers don't list, plus Sesko, Ugarte, Baleba and Rashford (counted); Shaw travelled but is a doubt, while Maguire is fit and expected to start, with Fernandes behind Zirkzee or Mount. Sporting are without Debast and Nuno Santos (counted) but have Ioannidis and Flavio back; Polish referee Szymon Marciniak (about 3.5 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals (1.7 Sporting, 1.1 United), already taking Sesko off United. Cunha's ban is not on their list and removes one of United's main creators and scorers, and Fonseca planning to sit deeper at times against a side under a brand-new coach points to a cagier game, so I lean a little lower, to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, fairly even (4.3 Sporting, 5.0 United). Sporting's low-block spells could give United more corners and Sporting fewer, which roughly cancels out, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, already taking about 9% off for Marciniak's record and 11% for Sporting's calm recent run, and adding a little for United's busier one. Both coaches expect a tense game but nothing in the news points to a rougher one than the records suggest, so I stay at 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.0 shots, lifted for both sides' recent shooting. Without Cunha United lose a player who shoots a lot from outside the box, and Sporting will defend deeper at times and look to counter, so I trim to about 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target, split evenly. Losing Cunha takes some quality out of United's attack and Shaw is a doubt on the left, while Sporting's side is close to full strength, so I trim to about 10.1.

401915816.overall: Kairat (27th of 36, two points) host Mjällby (9th, seven points and unbeaten in the competition) in Almaty and need a win to climb out of the elimination places, under interim coach Zhora Arutyunyan, who has promised changes to improve the attack after a 1-1 at Atalanta. Kairat's domestic season is over, so they have had about three weeks without a competitive game; their weak recent shooting and leaky defence (14 conceded in six, including 1-5 at home to Panathinaikos) are already in the numbers, and only Jorginho is listed out. Mjällby made a long trip via Istanbul, drew 1-1 with Malmö on Friday and still have a league finale on Sunday, so some rotation is likely; forward Jacob Bergström was reported out with a hamstring strain, and today's team-news page also lists keeper Wallinder and Helge as unavailable alongside the counted Dalsgaard and Stavitski. Polish referee Paweł Raczkowski's low card record (3.8 a game) is already counted. News today confirmed the picture rather than changing it, so the view holds.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already trim Kairat for scoring only 3 in their last six. Bergström, one of Mjällby's two top scorers, is reported out, which the numbers don't know, and Mjällby may rotate with a league game on Sunday, so I take a little off their side, to about 2.1. Kairat's three-week break and promised attacking changes pull both ways, so the size stays small.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, already cutting Kairat for winning only 12 in their last six and lifting Mjällby a little for 17 in their last three. Kairat should push at home as they need the win while Mjällby, the in-season side, keep the ball; the near-even split (4.4 to 4.2) already reflects that and the reported absences matter little for corners, so I stay at 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards, already taking a little off for referee Paweł Raczkowski (3.8 cards a game in six on record) and for Mjällby's tidy recent record. The clubs have never met and there is no rivalry; a Kairat side that must win could foul more if they fall behind, but that is only a hunch, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots and already take about 7% off Kairat for their low recent shooting. I trim a little more, to about 24.1, because Kairat have had no competitive game for around three weeks under an interim coach and Mjällby are without Bergström after a long trip with a league game on Sunday; the numbers can't see either.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already cutting Kairat by about 10% for only 14 on target in six and lifting Mjällby for their accurate recent shooting. With Bergström reported out and Kairat short of match rhythm, I go a bit lower, to about 8.0.

401915815.overall: Ajax (11th of 36, 6 points) host FC Thun (19th, 3 points) three days before Sunday's Klassieker at Feyenoord. Ajax have won six of their last seven, but midfielder Jorthy Mokio broke his fibula earlier this week, which the numbers' empty missing list does not know; Dolberg, Adingra and Tsygankov are long-term absences already in Ajax's form, and today's team-news page still lists Brandt and Gaaei as doubts, with Brandt widely expected to be saved for Feyenoord. Thun lost 3-2 at Young Boys, rotate a lot and also have a league game on Sunday; earlier reports had striker Furkan Dursun and midfielder Mattias Käit unlikely to play. cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, with Thun expected to collect more (2.7) as the side chasing the ball, but they had no referee to go on. shots.text: The numbers say 30.5 shots, about 20 of them for Ajax. With Brandt doubtful and likely rested, Mokio out and other regulars possibly saved for Feyenoord, plus Thun missing striker Dursun, I trim slightly to about 29.6; it is a mild lean because Ajax should still have most of the ball.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, 2.9 of them for Brighton, and already take Mitoma, Ferguson and Tzimas into account. A rotated Brighton side with Newcastle next, Minteh doubtful and Azeez out, against a settled, compact Craiova side, points slightly lower, so I go to about 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, 8.2 of them for Brighton, who should have long spells of possession against a Craiova side that defends deep with wing-backs dropping into a back five. That pattern drives corners whichever Brighton players start, so I stay at 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards and already add about 6% for referee Matthias Jöllenbeck, who has shown 5.3 cards a game in his three on record. shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, about 22 for Brighton. Struijk and Gomez are rested, Azeez, Yalcouye and Boscagli are out and Minteh is a doubt before Newcastle, none of which the numbers can see, so I trim to about 27.7; Brighton should still dominate the ball at home.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target and already cut Brighton for only 25 on target in their last six. A rotated Brighton side with Gomez rested and Minteh doubtful has fewer of its usual creators, so I go to about 10.0.

401915810.overall: Egnatia (26th of 36, 2 points) host Lincoln Red Imps (22nd, 3 points) in Tirana, still looking for a first win at this stage after two draws and a loss, with only two goals scored in three games; the club has sold cheap tickets and says it wants three points. goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and already add a little for Lincoln because Egnatia's regular defender Bitri is banned. Egnatia should attack at home in front of a bigger crowd, but their heavy rotation is already part of their recent form and Lincoln have a full squad, so I stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, 5.9 for Egnatia as the side expected to push, and they already count Lincoln's recent habit of conceding lots of corners and winning few. Nothing I found on lineups or tactics changes that picture, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, split evenly, and already lift Egnatia a little for the cards Lincoln's opponents have collected lately. Referee Oscar Johnson has no card record in the numbers and I found nothing on his style; with no rivalry between the clubs I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, two thirds of them for Egnatia, and already add about 10% for Egnatia because Lincoln have allowed many shots lately while cutting Lincoln for their own low shooting. shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. Lincoln report a full squad and Egnatia's absences (Bitri, Bakayoko and the players left out of the European squad) are already counted or already in their form, so I stay at 9.4.

401915811.overall: Hearts (32nd of 36, 1 point) host Monaco (4th, 9 points from 9) at a sold-out Tynecastle; Hearts have not won in Europe this season and need points, while Monaco are almost through. goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 1.9 for Monaco, and already take big cuts for Hearts without McEntee and for Monaco without Brunner, Golovin and Idumbo. Monaco's usual rotation is part of their form and Hearts' big win at Dundee came against weak opposition, so I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, nearly even, as Hearts tend to go direct and win set pieces at home while Monaco keep the ball. Nothing in the team news changes that, so I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already count referee Daniel Schlager, close to the average at 4.1 a game over 37 games. A loud Tynecastle and a Hearts side chasing the game could add a booking, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots and already trim Monaco for their lower recent shooting. Hearts are expected to keep a similar eleven and Monaco's rotation before Sunday's league game is normal for them, so I see no reason to move from 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, 5.1 for Monaco. The absences that matter on both sides are already counted and Monaco's extra one, Elebi, is a fringe defender, so I stay at 8.8.

401915813.overall: Iberia 1999 (29th of 36, 1 point) host Getafe (30th, 1 point) in Tbilisi; Iberia lean on striker Amiran Dzagania and a fairly settled side, while Getafe probably need wins here and at home to Inter Escaldes to reach the top 24. goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.7 for Getafe. Getafe have not scored in three games, Bordalás has openly put the league first with a must-win trip to Espanyol on Monday, and Andrés García and Romero are missing too, none of which the numbers see; I go to about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, 5.0 for Getafe, and already cut Iberia for winning only 4 in their last three. A rotated Getafe side still plays direct with crosses into the box, so the count should hold; I stay at 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards, already high because Getafe foul a lot, Iberia have picked up many cards lately and referee Horațiu Feșnic has shown 5.5 a game in his two on record. shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots, nearly 16 for Getafe, and already lift Getafe for their recent shot volume. A rotated Getafe side with league priorities and a blunt attack lately should be cautious, so I trim to about 23.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target. With Getafe likely to rest starters before Espanyol and without a goal in three games, and Juanmi and Uche out (already counted), I go a little lower, to about 7.8.

401915812.overall: Lugano top the Conference League table with 9 points from 3 games (11 scored, 4 conceded), while Jablonec are 23rd on 2 points with no win in Europe after 2-3 at Freiburg, 0-0 with Brighton and 1-1 at Riga. goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals but take about 16% off Lugano's scoring for Ajeti as suspended, while Swiss reports say his ban covers only domestic games and he is free for Thursday. corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners, 5.4 for Jablonec, who need a first European win and attack with crosses at home, with both sides' recent corner counts already in. Ajeti's return changes Lugano's finishing rather than how much of the ball they have, and a few rotated players should not change their wide play, so I stay at 9.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards, already adding about 6% for referee David Smajc (6.0 a game in two on record) and more for both sides' recent bookings. Ajeti's red card was in the Swiss league and these clubs have never met, so nothing points to an unusually heated game and I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots, a fairly open game, already lifted a little for Jablonec's recent volume. Ajeti's return helps Lugano's finishing more than their number of shots, and the rotation expected before Sunday pulls slightly the other way, so I stay at 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Jablonec's stand-in keeper Mihelak (Hanus is counted) and Ajeti's availability matter more for how many go in than for how many are on target, so I stay at 9.2.

401915739.overall: A Baltic meeting in Kaunas between Kauno Zalgiris, last of 36 with 0 points and a 1-11 goal record (0-4 at Brighton, 1-4 at home to Brann, 0-3 at Lugano), and Riga FC, 19th-20th after three 1-1 draws. shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target and already cut Zalgiris for only 4 on target in their last three. With no new injuries reported on either side and only Varslavans out (counted), I stay at 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, already low because both sides have been booked rarely lately and referee Ishmael Barbara shows 3.3 a game. There is nothing heated between these clubs, so I stay at 3.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target and already lift Brann (34 on target in six) and trim AGF (8 in three). Brann's side at KFUM was close to their best available, so nothing new moves it and I stay at about 10.4.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 2.3 for Besiktas, and already lift Besiktas for 15 goals in their last 6 (+4.2%) and for Marciano missing in Hapoel's goal (+6.2%). corners.text: The numbers say 7.3 corners, 4.7 for Besiktas, already trimmed slightly for both sides' recent corner counts. cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with Hapoel the more booked side, and already take 12% off for referee Morten Krogh's low card rate (2.9 a game). shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots, 19.0 for Besiktas, already nudged for recent form. Besiktas should keep shooting often against a weak defence with a reserve keeper, but a rotated front line after a tiring journey may take a little off their volume, so I go slightly lower, to about 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target, 7.7 for Besiktas, already lifted for sharp recent finishing (+3.9%) and trimmed for Hapoel (-5.8%). goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, 1.2 for Celta and 1.8 for Bournemouth, and already trim Celta for scoring only 4 in their last 6 (-4.2%). corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners, split fairly evenly. Giraldez wants a high tempo with Celta's wing-backs pushing on, and Bournemouth play direct and wide on the break; recent corner form is already in the numbers, so I stay at about 8.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already raised 14% for referee Harm Osmers (4.5 a game) and lowered for Bournemouth's few recent bookings. Bournemouth's aggressive press can cause fouls, but that is part of their record, and there is no rivalry here, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots and already raise Celta for shooting a lot lately (+8.3%), even if few go in. Celta without Iglesias still shoot often from range, Giraldez promises his strongest side and Bournemouth's front line is close to full strength, so I stay at about 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 on target and already cut Celta's share for poor accuracy (-9.6%), which largely reflects playing without Iglesias. Bournemouth keep their side up with Evanilson available and Kroupi not registered, so I stay at about 8.7.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 2.1 of them for Leverkusen. cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards and already take 17% off for referee Mykola Balakin, who averages 2.8 a game. The Maksimir crowd can raise the temperature in a game both sides need, but that is part of Dinamo's home record, so I stay at about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.9 shots and already lift Leverkusen for heavy recent shooting (+6.2%). shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 on target and already lift Leverkusen (+6.6%) after 45 on target in their last six. With the absences on both sides already in the missing list and Misic fit for Dinamo, I stay at about 10.

401915507.overall: Marseille (31st, 3 points) host Levski Sofia (10th, 7 points) at the Velodrome and need a win to keep play-off hopes alive; OM won at Leverkusen last time in Europe but then lost 3-2 at home to Le Mans from 2-0 up, and Genesio spoke of a mental and defensive fragility. goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, 2.5 for Marseille and 0.8 for Levski, and already lift Levski a little for Emerson's absence. goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals (1.5 Frosinone, 1.0 Parma); they take Raimondo and Birligea off Frosinone and Romero off Parma, and add both teams' leaky recent defending (Frosinone conceded 13 in six, Parma 12). corners.text: The numbers say 11.5 corners, 7.5 of them Frosinone's, and already add +16% for Frosinone's 53 corners in their last six games. Alvini's 4-2-3-1 with Ghedjemis and Kvernadze wide against a Parma side that sits in a 3-5-2 is the pattern the numbers already expect, so I stay at about 11.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.0 cards: they already take about 11% off for referee Kevin Bonacina's low count (3.2 a game) and some more because both teams have been booked less than usual lately. shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.1 shots on target and already add +20% for Frosinone's recent accuracy. Without their two main centre-forwards Frosinone should test the goalkeeper a little less, and Parma's attack without Romero is weak; a Parma defence without Diego Carlos limits the trim, so I go to about 10.8.

401884721.overall: Cologne (14th, 10 points, no win in five) host promoted Elversberg (9th, 13 points), who play an open, attacking game and have conceded 11 in their last five. goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and already take Cologne's absentees off, mainly Dallinga (about -11%), Skhiri and Castro-Montes. corners.text: The numbers say 11.1 corners, most of them Cologne's (7.1), and already count both teams' recent corner form. cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards; they already add about 25% for referee Sören Storks (4.8 cards a game) and some for both teams' recent bookings (Cologne 16 in six). This is not a derby or a heated fixture, so with the referee already counted I stay at 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots and already trim a few for Cologne's quieter recent attacking. Elversberg's open style should give Cologne room to shoot on the break, and Elversberg like to have the ball, which is how both teams usually play, so I stay at 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target and already reflect Cologne's recent attacking without Dallinga. Ache's return gives Cologne a proper centre-forward option off the bench, but nothing new changes the picture either way, so I stay at 8.8.

401884722.overall: Hamburg (12th) host Bayern (2nd) a week after a 4-0 Nordderby defeat at Werder Bremen; Muheim (muscle tear) and Poulsen are probably out for the rest of the year, and Lokonga, Nadir and Remberg are also out, while Vuskovic may make his first appearance. goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.2 of them Bayern's, and take Kane (about -15%), Saibari, Gnabry and Davies off Bayern, plus Poulsen and Lokonga off Hamburg. Olise, Bayern's other main creator and scorer, is no longer on their missing list although he has only just started running, and Bayern looked blunt at Lille three days earlier, so I take 7% off, to about 2.9; Hamburg losing Muheim and Musiala's return limit the cut.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Bayern will still have most of the ball and pin Hamburg back, and fewer wide attackers (Olise, Gnabry, Davies out) could mean a little less crossing, but Hamburg without left wing-back Muheim may concede more down the flanks, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards; they already take about 19% off for referee Bastian Dankert (3.2 a game) and some for Bayern's calm recent record, and add a little for past meetings. Hamburg will want a reaction after the derby defeat, but nothing points clearly up or down beyond what the numbers count, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.3 shots and already add 14% for Bayern's high recent shot count, which came with Kane and Olise in the side; their absences are counted on goals, not on shots. Bayern should still dominate but create less, as at Lille with Laimer as a makeshift striker, and they play two and a half days after that away game, so I take 6% off, to about 30.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, 7.1 of them Bayern's, without taking off Kane and Olise, their most accurate shooters (injuries are counted only on goals). Musiala and Díaz are back but short of match time, so I keep an 8% cut, to about 9.9.

401884723.overall: A relegation six-pointer: Mainz (13th, 10 points) have lost five competitive games in a row, the latest 3-1 at Augsburg after which fans whistled the team, and Urs Fischer said they get what they deserve. Union (17th, 7 points) were beaten 5-1 at home by Leipzig and Berlin papers call this an 'Endspiel' for coach Mauro Lustrinelli, a former assistant of Fischer's; Union have conceded 26 goals in 10 games, the worst at this stage in their Bundesliga history. goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals and already add for Van den Bosch's ban (about +6% to Mainz), take off for Juranovic (-8% to Union) and count the head-to-head. corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Mainz expected to have more (5.9) at home, and they already count Union's low recent corner count (20 in six). Union have switched between a back four and a back five without changing how much they attack down the flanks, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards; they already add about 12% for referee Timo Gerach (4.4 cards a game) and a little for both sides' recent bookings (Union 17 in six). They don't count the stakes: 13th against 17th, both on losing runs and Union's coach reportedly playing for his job, which points to a nervy, physical game, so I add 4%, to about 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots and already add about 12% to Mainz for how many shots Union have been conceding (110 in six). With Khedira and Uduokhai also missing from Union's defence, which the numbers don't know, Mainz should find a little more room, so I add 3%, to about 28.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. Mainz have been conceding plenty on target and Union create little, both already in the numbers; the extra gaps in Union's defence without Khedira and Uduokhai add a little for Mainz, so I go to about 9.3.

401884719.overall: Another relegation six-pointer between two promoted sides who struggle to score: Paderborn (15th, 10 points) host Schalke (16th, 7 points). Paderborn lost 4-0 at Leverkusen last time; their attack is described as harmless under coach Kettemann although the defence holds up, and striker Stefano Marino was reported hurt at Leverkusen but is still in the expected line-up, while Gayret and Awortwie-Grant are out. Schalke drew 0-0 with Stuttgart, are eight competitive games without a win, report no new injuries and have more options again (Becker or Gosens at left-back); Miron Muslic rejects calling it a must-win game. The numbers count Wöber's absence (-12% to Schalke's goals) and now referee Florian Exner (5.2 cards a game, +33%); I only add a few cards for the stakes.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.4 goals, already low because Schalke have scored only 2 in six, Paderborn rarely score either, and Wöber is taken off Schalke. Marino's knock is only one report and he is still expected to start, and Schalke have no new injuries, so I stay at 1.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners and already trim a little for both teams' recent form. Paderborn's back three with wing-backs Obermair and Curda and Schalke's 4-2-3-1 are how both usually line up, so nothing changes their style and I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.8 cards; they already add about a third for referee Florian Exner (5.2 a game) but take some off because both teams have been booked rarely lately (Paderborn 6 in six). A 15th-versus-16th game with points this tight is usually more physical than these teams' average, which the numbers don't count, so I add 4%, to about 2.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, with both teams' recent shot counts already in. Paderborn should be more open at home than at Leverkusen and Schalke have a full squad, but neither side creates much, so I stay at 28.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. Both attacks have been blunt for weeks, which is already part of their recent record, and nothing new changes that, so I stay at 8.6.

Nothing new points either way, so I stay at about 2.7.
