Leeds' wide play and crosses fit the home side winning most of them, and Lampard says Coventry must match Leeds physically rather than change their approach, so I stay at about 8.3.

cards.text: The numbers expect 2.7 cards, already counting Leeds being booked more than usual lately, Coventry less, and Paul Tierney's slightly low rate (3.8 a game). Lampard spoke of a rivalry with Leeds fans from his Chelsea and Derby days, but it is not a derby between the clubs and there are no bans in play, so I stay at about 2.7.

shots.text: The numbers expect 28.1 shots, 18.5 from Leeds at home, which already includes Leeds shooting more than usual lately. Leeds have a fully fit attack apart from Joseph, and Coventry lose Awoniyi, which the numbers already assume, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 8.4 shots on target: 5.2 for Leeds and 3.2 for Coventry. Leeds' sharper finishing and Awoniyi's absence are both already counted; with Wright still weeks away Coventry rely on Cherif or Simms up front, which fits the low away figure, so I stay at about 8.4.

401879226.overall: Manchester United are 19th, winless in nine league games, and Mauricio Pochettino is still looking for his first win after a 4-0 loss at Liverpool and a chaotic 2-2 draw at Sporting on Wednesday night, where Bruno Fernandes scored twice and Youri Tielemans was sent off (a European ban, not a league one). That leaves United barely three days to recover; Amad Diallo went off with a knock in Lisbon, Sesko, Ugarte and Baleba are out, Rashford is close but unconfirmed and Luke Shaw is a doubt. Reports differ on Leny Yoro: most say his Anfield red card was overturned, one still lists him as banned. goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 1.6 for United and 1.4 for Brentford, already counting United's leaky defence, Brentford's scoring and Thiago's ban (about -10%). Amad's knock is a small worry for United and Callum Wilson starting for Brentford is a small step down; these roughly cancel, so I stay at about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.4 corners: 5.9 for United and 4.4 for Brentford, with form and past meetings counted. A home side chasing a first win under Pochettino should push forward, which fits that split, and the team news does not change it, so I stay at about 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.4 cards, already including Robert Jones' above-average rate (4.4 a game) and United's rising card count. Tielemans' red card was in the Champions League, so it does not stop him playing here, and it is not a derby, so I stay at about 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers expect 29.3 shots, 18.7 of them from United. United played a draining 2-2 in Lisbon on Wednesday night and have about three days to recover, with Amad carrying a knock, which the numbers do not count. Brentford's absences are already in, so I take only about 3% off, to about 28.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 9.8 shots on target, helped by how many United have allowed lately. Thiago's ban is already counted; I keep a small 2% cut for United's tired legs after Lisbon and Amad's knock, to about 9.6.

Excelsior under Ruben den Uil ended a run of four defeats (including 0-9 at Twente) with a 3-2 win at Feyenoord on 21 November, their first league win in De Kuip since 1980, with on-loan winger Aymen Sliti outstanding and Widell heading the winner from a corner. Danny Makkelie referees, as the numbers already assume (about 2.5 cards a game); news for this match was thin, with no full preview found two days out.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and already add Telstar's 14 goals and Excelsior's 22 conceded in their last six. They also add about +6% to Excelsior for Gerald Alders being out and take about 3.5% off Telstar for Rui Mendes, but neither is on the latest injury list, so both look available. Undoing those two nets out to a hair lower, so I move it 1%, to about 3.37.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners and already trim Excelsior's share for their few corners lately (19 in six). Excelsior did score the winner at Feyenoord from a corner and defended deep for the last 20 minutes there, but at home against a fellow struggler they should have more of the ball; nothing on tactics or line-ups points clearly either way, so I stay at about 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.4 cards and already take about 12% off for Danny Makkelie, who books about 2.5 per game, and a little off Telstar for fewer cards lately. This is a six-pointer between two teams in the bottom five and the numbers carry no stakes adjustment for it, so I lean mildly higher, to about 2.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots and already move Excelsior down (-12.5%) and Telstar up (+9.9%) for recent form. Excelsior's win at Feyenoord showed life in their attack with Sliti in form, while Telstar had plenty of long-range efforts against PEC; with Mendes and Alders apparently fit and Seedorf, out for two weeks already, still doubtful, these roughly balance, so I stay at about 26.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target and already count Excelsior's poor accuracy lately (12 on target in six) and Telstar's better run (37). PEC's keeper saved all of Telstar's long shots last week, which fits that pattern; nothing new on either attack beyond what the form figures show, so I stay at about 9.9.

Ntoi's likely return helps Rio Ave's back line while Vrousai's status is unclear, and Seabra's planned changes are not named yet; nothing points clearly either way, so I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 5.6 to 4.1 for Arouca, already lifting Arouca a little because Rio Ave have conceded 36 corners in their last six. Rio Ave need a win more than Arouca and could push their full-backs on, but they have lost four in a row playing that way; I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards, already adding a little for referee Diogo Rosa (5.7 a game, small sample) and Rio Ave's booking rate, and trimming Arouca because Rio Ave have drawn few fouls lately. shots.text: The numbers say 23.6 shots and already take about 14% off Rio Ave, who managed only 51 shots in their last six, and add about 7% to Arouca against a Rio Ave side that has allowed 93. Seabra knows Arouca's players well and may change his XI, but no names are out, so I stay at 23.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target, with small form changes already in. Arouca's defence has been one of the league's best this season, which the numbers see, and Rio Ave's possible return of Ntoi only restores their usual back line; I stay at 8.5.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.0 goals and already add about 6% each to Moreirense for Pacheco's ban and keeper Lucas Franca being out, and take about 7% off them for Parsemain. corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners, split almost evenly, and already trim both sides for low recent corner counts (Moreirense 17 and Santa Clara 19 in their last six). A new Santa Clara back line might concede a few more set pieces, but Moreirense have not been winning many corners lately, so I stay at 8.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, already adding about 5% for referee Luis Carlos Mateus Filipe (6.3 a game in a small sample) and 6% for Santa Clara's 22 cards in their last six, and trimming Moreirense for only 9. Inexperienced Santa Clara defenders could be drawn into fouls, but that is a hunch and the referee is already counted, so I stay at 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.6 shots, already adding about 7% to Moreirense and 6% to Santa Clara for recent shooting and defending. I add a little more, to about 23.5, because Moreirense should test a Santa Clara defence missing three regulars, only one of them counted, and Parsemain and Tiago Andrade give them more attacking options.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 6.4 shots on target, trimmed for both sides' modest recent accuracy. 401876394.overall: Angers are 17th with 8 points from 11 games under Stephane Gilli and have taken one point from their last five league games (2 scored, 13 conceded). Lens are 11th with 14 points and lost 3-1 at RB Leipzig on Tuesday, their fourth Champions League defeat in a row; captain Florian Thauvin, their top scorer and assist maker (7 goals, 9 assists), cut short a TV interview afterwards but apologised on Wednesday, said he is staying until the end of the season, and the club will not sanction him, so he is expected to start. goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, Lens 1.5 and Angers 0.9; they already take off Edouard, Aguilar and Cuisance (about -12% for Lens) and know Angers have scored 3 in their last 6. Thauvin has apologised and should play, and Zinga's absence from one training session is not explained, so I stay at about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, 5.3 for Lens and 4.7 for Angers. Lens had 9 corners and most of the ball against Toulouse and Angers sit deep when behind, but that pattern is already in the recent counts the numbers use, so I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards: referee Romain Lissorgue (4.2 a game) adds about 8%, while both sides' calm recent card counts take some off. Angers' relegation worry and Lens' frustration could add edge, but there is no history of needle in this fixture, so I stay at about 3.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already reflecting Elche's 16 cards in their last six and Atletico's quieter run. No referee has been named yet, and a relegation-threatened home side against a top-three team brings intensity the numbers already see. I stay at about 4.2.

401884726.overall: Eighth-placed Stuttgart (13 pts from 10) host seventh-placed Frankfurt (15 pts) on Saturday at 18:30, both unbeaten in their last three league games and chasing the European places. corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, already lifting Frankfurt (+5%) for their 35 corners in the last six. Stuttgart's full-strength wide players (Leweling, Führich, Mittelstädt) are what the numbers expect at home, so I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, already nudged up for both teams' busier recent card counts. No referee has been named and the match has no derby edge beyond the race for Europe, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.3 shots, already raising Frankfurt by almost 19% because Stuttgart allowed 107 shots in their last six. shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target, already raising Frankfurt (+10%) for their recent accuracy and trimming Stuttgart slightly. shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already lifted for Inter's heavy recent shooting (+15.8%). cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, already lifted about 7% for referee Geoffrey Kubler and counting both sides' recent cards, but they have no stakes flag for this game. shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, already boosted because Le Havre have been shooting a lot lately (96 in six) even while losing. Strasbourg's missing forwards (Panichelli, Balde) have been out for weeks and are in their form, so I stay at 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target, about level between the sides. Both defences are weakened by long-term injuries that the recent numbers already show, and a doubtful Strasbourg goalkeeper does not change how many shots are on target, so I stay at about 9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, 4.4 of them for Lille. Without Ueda and with tired legs or a changed front line after Bayern, Lille's finishing should be a little blunter than the numbers assume, so I lean slightly lower, 8.2 to about 7.9.
